newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soy prices show independent strength-Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soy prices show independent strength-Safras.

text.p: Brazilian domestic soybean prices fell last week in tandem with a sharp drop in Chicago futures but are beginning to show signs of independent strength, independent consultants Safras e Mercado said.
"The reduction was not proportional and one could observe the first signs of separation between internal prices and the CBOT, which is natural between harvests," Safras said in a weekly report.
This was happening earlier than usual this year due to the high volume of soybeans already exported, which was squeezing domestic supply, it added.
Soybean prices in Cascavel fell to 15.40 reais ($14.25) per 60-kg bag, down 11 percent from a month ago. In Passo Fundo, prices were down 15 percent while in Rondonopolis they fell 14 percent.
Prices were unlikely to recover to the same levels as registered earlier this year but should at least partially recuperate as domestic supply tightens, Safras said.
"The bigger problem will be observed on the liquidity front, since factories should stop earlier this year because of a lack of product, especially those located further from ports," it said.
